newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia to place 10 shares in Euro CESI index.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia to place 10 shares in Euro CESI index.

text.p: Slovenia's Stock Exchange said on Wednesday it will place ten of its shares in the Central European Share Index (CESI) from October 31.
"The shares that will be included in CESI currently represent about 89 percent of the capitalisation of our main market," Tomaz Rotar, deputy executive of the Ljubljana bourse, told Reuters.

He said CESI would include the shares of banks SKB and Probanka, drug company Lek's issue A, warehousing firm BTC, food producers Kolinska and Droga, health resort operator Terme Catez, brokerage Nika, pharmaceutical trader Salus and ordinary shares of bank Dolenjska banka.
On September 30 the capitalisation of the Ljubljana main market amounted to $567 million.
"Our shares will represent about 2.3 percent of the capitalisation of CESI," Rotar said.
He said the Ljubljana bourse expected to include more Slovenian shares in the CESI on April 30, 1997, when the index would be changed again.
"We expect to enlarge CESI then with shares of some newly privatised companies that will be listed in the meantime," Rotar said.
Currently there are 24 companies listed on the main market of the Ljubljana bourse.
